s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with migration to the right lower quadrant
salient_findings: Abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
key_facts: Abdominal pain began around the umbilicus 2 days prior
Pain migrated to the right lower quadrant
Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
Ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis
Computed tomography showed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Classic presentation of abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings compatible with appendicitis

shortlist.label: Plastron appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound assessment specifically mentioned as compatible with plastron appendicitis, which is a type of appendicitis

shortlist.label: Perforated appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays and elevated white-cell count, which could indicate a perforation

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and elevated white-cell count, with a possible linear lesion on computed tomography that could represent a Meckel's diverticulum

shortlist.label: Epiploic appendagitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and tenderness in the right lower quadrant, with a possible association with the linear lesion on computed tomography

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain that migrated to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings, are consistent with acute appendicitis. The ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis and computed tomography showing a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Plastron appendicitis
rejected.why: While the ultrasound assessment was compatible with plastron appendicitis, this term is not a standard medical diagnosis and the overall clinical picture is more consistent with acute appendicitis.

rejected.label: Perforated appendicitis
rejected.why: There is no free air under the diaphragm on plain abdominal X-rays, which makes perforation less likely.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: The location of the pain and imaging findings are more consistent with appendicitis than Meckel's diverticulitis.

rejected.label: Epiploic appendagitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not support a diagnosis of epiploic appendagitis, which typically presents with more localized pain and different imaging characteristics.
